analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: a new EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift (425 lines) and a one-line switch-case edit in EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift (line 312, `.toolCall, .toolCallDelta: continue`). No production code, key handling, attestation, coordinator protocol, or cache-storage code is changed in the supplied units, so no regression to the threat-model assets or trust boundaries is introduced here.

The new tests exercise prefill-geometry policy that lives in EngineV2Factory. That code is not supplied. It covers chunk and step-budget env overrides, the Gemma 4 media block floor, and paged-pool ring sizing from max(chunk, stripe). The tests disable the prefix cache (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0) and pass a KV backend guard path of /dev/null. They use tiny synthetic models and stub tokenizers, with no real secrets, keys, or prompts. The T-041 prefix-cache/SSD tier is not touched. The tests do not change the cache gate, TTL, lookup HMAC, or AAD behavior, and they run with the cache off.

The tests assert fail-toward-SDK behavior on malformed chunk and budget values, and that undersized Gemma 4 overrides are raised to cover a whole media block. That is availability-oriented hardening against a ring-precondition trap, and it is only tested here. The test at lines 182-184 asserts saturating arithmetic for Int.max, which is relevant to overflow safety. The production implementation was not supplied, so whether the wider default Gemma chunk (2048) changes memory peaks or DoS exposure (T-010/T-029-style availability) depends on unseen EngineV2Factory code. The .toolCallDelta case implies a production enum change elsewhere in the PR. The test merely ignores it, and the tool-call streaming path and its encryption (T-008) should be reviewed in the units that contain that change.

Remaining integration questions: confirm the production EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry implementation matches these tests, and confirm that the new toolCallDelta stream events are encrypted on the response path.
